reason: E1 and E3 show that protective oxide glaze layers form on similar HEA systems during high-temperature wear, supporting the tribofilm premise. However, no cited evidence addresses the specific AlCrFeCoNi composition, the self-healing or nanocrystalline nature of the film, or the proposed oxygen partial pressure control experiment.
premises: Sliding wear of AlCrFeCoNi HEA coatings in oxygen-rich environments forms a protective, self-healing nanocrystalline oxide tribofilm.
This tribofilm reduces wear by minimizing direct metal contact and localizing plastic deformation.
Tribo-oxidation kinetics are active and beneficial at 200–500°C.
Varying oxygen partial pressure will control tribofilm formation and thus wear rate.
